claim: Cognitive ethnography takes the whole socio-technical system (people plus artifacts) as the unit of cognitive analysis, and shows that artifacts change the task rather than just storing information (the speed bug turns a memory and reading task into a perceptual match).
agent_test: Compare an agent whose notes and checklists are task-transforming media (a pre-computed target card checked by matching) against plain log notes, at equal tokens.

claim: The cockpit speed-memory account rests on one author's qualitative observation (100+ observer flights over 6 years). There are no error counts, no crews with and without bugs, and no independent replication found. Gap search: checklists (a related artifact) do lower errors in before-after studies (deaths 1.5% to 0.8%) but a 101-hospital natural experiment found no significant effect (OR 0.91, P=0.13).
agent_test: Not testable on the agent directly. Treat distributed-cognition design claims as hypotheses and run A/B tests on artifact design.

claim: Work is spread across people, time and representation formats: compute in low workload and use later; convert visual to spoken so a busy partner gets the cue; keep several redundant representations (card, speech, bug).
agent_test: Two-phase agent: an early planning pass writes target values to a scratch file; a later pass only compares. Compare error rate with a one-pass agent at equal tokens.

claim: Distributed cognition, situated action (Suchman) and extended mind are partly rivals and partly complements. The disagreement is conceptual; no quantitative test pits them against each other.
agent_test: No cheap test; skip.

claim: A general-purpose VLM alone matches humans on video annotation on average (mean human-normalised score 97.0) but is very uneven by task: attention coding 17.8, sign recognition 35.4, mistake handling 47.0, against communicative intent 134.0 and co-speech gesture 128.4.
agent_test: Run the agent on a mixed task set and report per-task results, not only the mean.

claim: Human verification of VLM labels beats either alone on average (HNS 121.5), cuts human time 48.9% and cost 31-45%, with biggest gains where the VLM was worst. It lowered scores on two tasks (behavior interval 101.6 to 86.5, animal behavior 110.8 to 90.5). Gap search: the paper itself warns about anchoring on a plausible VLM output, untested; LLM self-verification without outside signal also flips right answers to wrong (Huang 2024).
agent_test: Agent verifies a first pass vs solves fresh, at equal tokens. Look for tasks where verification anchors errors.

claim: GPT-4 reproduces human qualitative codes well for simple codebooks and poorly for hard ones: kappa 0.94-0.97 (task A), 0.74-0.75 (B), 0.55-0.58 (C). GPT-3.5 is worse and invented 47 codes outside the codebook (GPT-4: 2).
agent_test: Measure the invented-category rate of our agent under closed label sets, with and without a stay-in-list guardrail.

claim: LLM annotation can beat crowd workers on accuracy and cost for text classification (about +25 points, under $0.003 per item, n=6,183 over 4 datasets); a one-task GPT-4 study found the LLM beat experts and individual crowd workers.
agent_test: Agent annotates with majority of k reruns vs a single run at equal tokens.

claim: Repeated LLM thematic coding is fairly stable but model-dependent (kappa across runs 0.84-0.91, widest range for Claude). Expert confidence in LLM coding is self-reported, not accuracy.
agent_test: Run the same coding 5 times, measure kappa, and compare consensus-of-runs against a single run.

claim: Memory with observation, reflection and planning raises rated believability of agents: full 29.89 vs no reflection 26.88 vs none 21.21 (TrueSkill, 100 raters). The raters ranked interview answers, not task success. Memory had embellishment failures (6 of 453, 1.3%).
agent_test: Ablate the reflection step in agent memory at equal tokens on a long task and measure task success.

claim: Cognitive Workspace reports 54-60% memory reuse and effect sizes up to d=196, but the metric is the paper's own, RAG scores 0 by construction, the corpus is 8 documents and the model GPT-3.5. Weak.
agent_test: Replicate with an answer-quality score before using.

claim: Interview-grounded LLM simulations of real people replicate individual survey answers well (GSS 72.8% vs retest 79.5% in the later version) but not incentivised economic games. Headline numbers differ between paper versions. Gap search: earlier text shows games normalised correlation 0.66 interview vs 0.48 demographic, ANOVA p=0.16; Twin-2K-500 gives 87.67% of retest on average.
agent_test: Check whether persona prompts help the agent on behaviour questions, not just self-report.

claim: Structured roles and SOPs in multi-agent setups beat unstructured ones on code tasks (MetaGPT HumanEval 85.9%, executability 3.75 of 4), but later multi-agent gains over single-agent chain of thought are modest (+4 to +5 points) and cost more tokens. Gap search: at matched token budgets multi-agent ranges +80.8% to -70.0% by task (Kim 2026); Shang v3 gains (+5 to +6) use 14,323 tokens vs 643 for CoT.
agent_test: Single agent with role-switching passes vs multi-agent at equal total tokens.

claim: People offload to LLMs in distinct profiles (N=97; clusters of 51/22/17/7 by volume); heavy offloading goes with the AI doing more of the essay. This is a human-side analogue of distributed cognition.
agent_test: Not an agent test; relevant to human-agent team design.

claim: No study was found that applies Hutchins-style cognitive ethnography to LLM agents, and no replication of the founding ethnographies appeared. The absence comes from a rate-limited search and is weak.
agent_test: Label agent traces for who or what holds which state at each step, then test design changes from the labels.

claim: Checklists, the nearest tested analogue of task-transforming artifacts, cut errors in before-after studies (Haynes: death 1.5% to 0.8%, complications 11.0% to 7.0%, N=3733/3955; Pronovost: infections 7.7 to 1.4 per 1000 catheter-days) but a large mandate natural experiment found no effect (Ontario, 101 hospitals, OR 0.91, P=0.13). No controlled test of the cockpit speed bug exists in what I could reach.
agent_test: A/B an agent with a pre-computed check card versus none, and also measure whether the card is actually used at each step.

claim: Reading agent traces ethnographically works as a design method: MAST (150+ traces, kappa 0.88) led to ChatDev fixes of +9.4 to +15.6 points (ProgramDev-v0 25.0 to 40.6) and AG2 +5 points, but tokens were not matched and an LLM cannot yet do the attribution (Who&When: 53.5% agent, 14.2% step).
agent_test: Code 50 own traces for who holds which state, change the design, rerun at equal tokens.

claim: Second-pass verification is not reliably safe. Self-verification without an external signal flips correct answers to wrong ones (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1); human verification of VLM labels hurt on 2 of 15 tasks and the authors suspect anchoring. Anchoring is plausible but not directly tested.
agent_test: Run verification blind to the first answer versus shown the first answer, same tokens, and compare accuracy.

claim: At matched token budgets multi-agent systems do not generally beat one agent: debate often loses to self-consistency (9 benchmarks, 4 models) and a 260-configuration study found +80.8% to -70.0% depending on task, with planning always worse. Single agent above about 45% accuracy gains nothing from more agents.
agent_test: Compare one agent role-switching against a multi-agent version at equal total tokens on a sequential task and a decomposable task.

claim: Shang et al. 2026 is verified in the published v3: gains of about +5.1 to +6.0 points on LiveBench subtasks with Holm-tested significance, but it uses 14,323 output tokens versus 643 for CoT, so no equal-token advantage is shown; it loses on instruction-following.
agent_test: Rerun against self-consistency at 14k tokens.

claim: Reflection beats plain episodic memory on task success in the originating lab (Reflexion HotPotQA +8 points absolute; HumanEval 91 vs 80) and an independent lab shows agents copy stored experiences so errors propagate. Rater-ranked believability (Park 2023) is not task success. No clean other-lab replication of the ablation found.
agent_test: Ablate reflection and memory filter on a task with unit tests, report pass rate.

claim: LLM coding accuracy is shown here only for closed codebooks (GPT-3.5 guessed on 4 of 13 tweet codes, fair to substantial kappa for GPT-3). Kappa on open codebooks and the rate of invented categories for current models stayed unmeasured in this search.
agent_test: Measure invented-code rate on open coding of 30 traces.
